metadata.title: How Chinese Taipei used TIMSS data to reform mathematics education

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This Compass brief synthesizes TIMSS 2003 and TIMSS 2011 results (and references PISA 2012) to describe policy processes in Chinese Taipei; it does not report an original student-level statistical or ML analysis with an explicit analytic dataset extract. As a result, the brief does not specify whether TIMSS sampling weights or replicate weights were applied, nor does it name any weight variables from the TIMSS international database. For analysts using TIMSS microdata, complex survey design features (stratification, clustering, and sampling weights) should be respected when estimating achievement and attitude indicators, and PV-based achievement scales should be analyzed using the TIMSS-provided plausible values with appropriate combining rules. The brief’s tables present benchmark-category percentages and country mean scores, which are typically derived from IEA’s scaling and reporting procedures rather than from a re-estimation described in this document.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: The document is a policy-oriented synthesis/brief that reports descriptive benchmark-category percentages and country mean scores from TIMSS (and references PISA), rather than fitting a student-level model that requires explicit plausible-value (PV) handling choices. Because no original PV-based achievement modeling is conducted in this brief, PV handling and missing-data handling strategies are not documented as part of an empirical estimation pipeline. This is therefore a reporting/analysis-scope mismatch rather than a methodological omission for an ML study.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used TIMSS 2003 and TIMSS 2011 published results for Chinese Taipei and four other East Asian comparison systems (Hong Kong, Japan, Singapore, South Korea) as presented in the brief’s tables; no student-level analytic subsample construction or exclusion criteria are described in the document.

data.outcome_summary: This IEA Compass brief explains how Chinese Taipei used successive TIMSS cycles as an evidence base for mathematics education reform rather than reporting a new empirical ML model. It highlights TIMSS 2003 patterns at grades 4 and 8—especially a higher share of students in the “below intermediate” benchmark group and a larger proportion reporting low confidence and low enjoyment in mathematics compared with the international average. These findings motivated the 2006 “After Class Support” policy, with stated targets for reducing low achievers and increasing the share of students who “like” mathematics by TIMSS 2011. The brief reports that TIMSS 2011 showed only small declines in the below-intermediate group and persistent gaps in enjoyment and confidence, leading to a policy shift toward the 2014 “Just Do Math” program. It also notes that TIMSS 2019 is planned to evaluate the program’s true success, while acknowledging that the brief’s evidence is descriptive and policy-process oriented rather than causal.

It does not provide an original student-level dataset, analytic sample sizes, PV/missing-data handling, or any ML model training/evaluation; therefore fields such as total_students, per-country n_students, and ML techniques are not applicable to the extraction target.
